story: On this bright, partly cloudy Wednesday just past noon, Gary, Donna, and Hal are gathered on Magnolia Loop, where Gary is eager to show his wiring sketches for a parade cart before Saturday. Donna is cheerfully pointing Hal toward her trimmed flamingo flock, which she has kept under the three-ornament limit, while Hal sets about tallying them in his notebook with quiet determination. Meanwhile, Rosa is at her house checking that her Thursday evening stays free so she won't get called into a shift, and she's hoping the afternoon sketching session goes well.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Double-check Thursday evening is clear so I can't be called in

gary.thought_process: Donna already told me the committee notice will post on the bulletin board any day now and suggested I ask Hal too. I said I'd grab my sketches and head to the rec center, but I haven't actually asked Hal anything yet. He's right here counting flamingos, probably for a law-compliance notebook, and he's the kind of fella who'd know the committee schedule. A quick question to Hal, then I can go rally with Donna and stop fretting about the cart lights review.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Hal. You know when the Architectural Review committee meets next? I've got wiring sketches for my parade cart ready to go and I'd like to get them in front of them before Saturday.

donna.thought_process: Gary has agreed to practice and is grabbing his sketches, so I shouldn't ask him again. Hal just showed up and is counting my flamingos from the street, which actually matters since L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. I'm a little nervous after my earlier flamingo overreach. Best move is to greet Hal, be upfront about the count, and mention the parade sketching at Rosa's, which also answers Gary's committee-date question as far as I know it.

parameters.content: Hal, welcome! Count away, I trimmed the flamingos down to stay under the three-ornament limit. Rosa's expecting us to sketch the parade cart this afternoon, and Gary wants to know when Architectural Review meets next, if you've heard.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with notebook in hand, and the flamingo flock is right here. I noted at Tick 241 I was counting them. Rather than take Donna's word, I should log the actual count for the committee. Gary and Donna are heading to the rec center anyway, so no need to chat. Let me interact with the flamingo flock and tally them for tomorrow's nine o'clock meeting.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday midday and I've already locked in Thursday evening, written the supper menu, and laid out paper, pencils, and the rules checklist on the dining table. Nobody's nearby to talk to. The one loose end is the shopping list, so I should interact with the kitchen again only if it moves things forward. Rather than repeat myself, I'll do a last pass through my shift schedule to confirm Thursday is truly clear, so I don't have to cancel on Donna and Hal. After that I can head out to the Loop to start gathering supplies and remind the neighbors.

parameters.content: Double-check Thursday evening is clear so I can't be called in

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
